condition.purpose: Verify the specified evidence of actual rent receipt and continuing lease term when actual rents exceed market rents.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the rent evidence and lease agreements for actual rents, market rents, receipt history, and lease term.
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Determine whether actual rents exceed market rents.

Step 3 - Validation and Verification: If actual rents exceed market rents, verify documentation of two (2) consecutive months proof of rental income receipt and lease agreement(s) to continue at a minimum of three (3) months after closing. Verify that security deposit does not count towards receipt and that rents are not prepaid.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Record whether the stated actual-rent evidence and lease conditions are met. Do not resolve whether STD-3.5 or STD-3.6 governs.
checks: When actual rents exceed market rents, evidence documents two (2) consecutive months proof of rental income receipt and lease agreement(s) to continue at a minimum of three (3) months after closing; security deposit is not counted towards receipt, and rents are not prepaid.

outcomes.criterion: When actual rents exceed market rents, all stated evidence and lease conditions are met.
Actual rents exceed market rents and the required evidence or lease conditions remain to be obtained or cleared.
Actual rents exceed market rents and the stated evidence or lease conditions are not met.
Actual rents do not exceed market rents.

condition.purpose: Determine whether documentation supports that excessive monthly rent reflected on the lease is typical for the area.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the lease for monthly rent and review any documentation submitted to support typical rent for the area.
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Determine whether the property is a single-family investment property and whether the lease reflects excessive monthly rent payments.

Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Verify that documentation supporting that the monthly rent is typical for the area is provided. Acceptable documentation may include classified ads from local newspapers, a Form 1007 completed by the appraiser, or a market rent survey completed by a local real estate company or rental management company familiar with market rents in the area.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Record whether the stated rent-support requirement is met.
checks: If a single-family investment property's lease reflects excessive monthly rent payments, documentation supporting that the monthly rent is typical for the area is provided.

outcomes.criterion: If the stated trigger applies, documentation supporting that the monthly rent is typical for the area is provided.
There is no case for this outcome.
The stated trigger applies and documentation supporting that the monthly rent is typical for the area is not provided.
The property is not a single-family investment property, or its lease does not reflect excessive monthly rent payments.

condition.purpose: Determine whether a loan on a property listed for sale in the last six months meets the stated appraisal-based maximum LTV/CLTV and related loan characteristics.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the appraisal report and listing history for appraised value, the last date listed, and the lowest recent listing price.
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Determine whether the property has been listed for sale in the last six months, measured from the last date of being listed to the Application Date.

Step 3 - Validation and Verification: If the property meets the listing-period test, verify that the loan meets the stated characteristics: the property is not in default or otherwise delinquent on lien(s); for investment properties, the subject is occupied by a tenant and is not vacant; the loan qualifies as either ≥ 1.0 DSCR or 43% maximum DTI; a prepayment penalty of at least three (3) years is present unless the property is in a state that does not allow prepayment penalties; twenty-four (24) months of reserves are present, with cash-in-hand considered if otherwise consistent with the Guide; the term is fully amortizing and not interest only; maximum LTV / CLTV is 65% based on the lesser of appraised value or lowest recent listing price; no subordinate financing is present; and impounds are present.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Record whether the listing-period test and all applicable stated loan characteristics are met.
checks: The property has been listed for sale in the last six months, measured from the last date of being listed to the Application Date.
For a property meeting the listing-period test, the property is not in default or otherwise delinquent on lien(s).
For an investment property meeting the listing-period test, the subject is occupied by a tenant and is not vacant.
For a property meeting the listing-period test, the loan qualifies as either ≥ 1.0 DSCR or 43% maximum DTI.

For a property meeting the listing-period test, no subordinate financing is present.
For a property meeting the listing-period test, impounds are present.

condition.purpose: Determine whether the property type and transaction meet the printed CLTV limits and eligibility restriction.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the appraisal report for property type and any property-specific classification relevant to the printed caps.
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Identify the property type, transaction purpose, and whether the property is in Florida or LTV is above 80.00%.

Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Verify the applicable printed cap: Non-Warrantable Condo — 80% purchase, 75% refinance R/T, 75% refinance C/O, with -5% CLTV for Florida properties and Min DSCR: 1.0; Condotel / PUDtel — 75% purchase, 70% refinance R/T, 65% refinance C/O, with -5% CLTV for Florida properties and Min DSCR: 1.0; 2-4 Unit — Max CLTV: 80%; Manufactured Home — 65% purchase, 60% refinance R/T, 60% refinance C/O. Verify that above 80.00% LTV only SFR, Warrantable Condos outside of Florida, Townhome and PUD are eligible.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Record whether the applicable printed cap and above-80.00% LTV eligibility restriction are met.
checks: For a Non-Warrantable Condo, CLTV does not exceed 80% for purchase, 75% for refinance R/T, or 75% for refinance C/O, with -5% CLTV for Florida properties; Min DSCR: 1.0.
For a Condotel / PUDtel, CLTV does not exceed 75% for purchase, 70% for refinance R/T, or 65% for refinance C/O, with -5% CLTV for Florida properties; Min DSCR: 1.0.
For a 2-4 Unit property, CLTV does not exceed Max CLTV: 80%.
For a Manufactured Home, CLTV does not exceed 65% for purchase, 60% for refinance R/T, or 60% for refinance C/O.
Above 80.00% LTV, the property is only SFR, Warrantable Condo outside of Florida, Townhome or PUD.

outcomes.criterion: The applicable property-type cap, its printed conditions, and the above-80.00% LTV eligibility restriction are met.
There is no case for this outcome.
An applicable property-type cap or printed condition is not met, or a property above 80.00% LTV is not one of the eligible property types.
No listed property-type cap or above-80.00% LTV restriction applies.

condition.purpose: Determine whether the required Form 1007 has been provided for a DSCR transaction or an applicable single-family transaction.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the appraisal report for a Form 1007 and identify the property type and transaction information.
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Determine whether the transaction is a DSCR transaction or a single-family transaction that meets one of the stated Form 1007 triggers.
Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Verify that a required Form 1007 is provided. If a Form 1007 is provided, verify that it is from the original appraiser or any state licensed appraiser.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Record whether the applicable Form 1007 requirement is met.
checks: A Form 1007 is provided for every DSCR transaction.

STD-5.6 Assets held / foreign accounts must be verified in U.S. Dollar equivalency at the current exchange rate via www.xe.com or the Wall Street Journal conversion table. \[G §3.10, p. 6\]

STD-5.7 Sufficient funds to close must be on deposit with the Escrow / Closing Agent at least three (3) business days (including Saturdays for this calculation) prior to any closing date. \[G §3.10, p. 6\]

STD-5.8 A copy of the two (2) most recent statements of that account is required. If the funds are not seasoned a minimum of sixty (60) days, a letter of explanation is required along with the information to comprise a sixty (60) day chain of funds. Bank statements in any language other than English must be translated into English. \[G §3.10, p. 6\]

STD-5.9 Per §8.4, Foreign Nationals, regardless of LTV / CLTV, need to document a minimum of 60 days seasoning, and funds held in a foreign bank / currency must be repatriated at minimum three (3) business days prior to Closing (STD-9.5). \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

STD-9.1 Gift funds, investment property or second homes: applicant(s) are required to contribute a portion of their own sourced and seasoned funds to the transaction at a minimum of 10% of the purchase price. Gift documentation requirements are in the Seller's Guide gift-fund section (Appendix B). \[G §8.7, p. 12; S: Loan Amount\]

STD-9.2 Verification of the seasoning of funds to close is required on loans over 70% CLTV for consumer transactions, or business purpose loans where funds to close are over \$50,000 and over 70% CLTV. Whether any loan on this program is a consumer transaction: Acra confirmation requested → Q-27. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

STD-9.3 Where the account(s) serving as the source of funds must be verified, verification may include a copy of the borrower's bank statement(s) for the most recent month(s), or a VOD reflecting a current and average balance for the most recent month(s). \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

STD-9.4 “All transactions require a minimum of 30-days documentation.” Whether any seasoning period applies to domestic funds beyond this documentation minimum: Acra confirmation requested → Q-12. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

STD-9.5 “In contrast to the above, but consistent with §3.10.1 of this Guide, funds held in a foreign bank / currency will need to be repatriated at minimum three (3) business days prior to Closing and Foreign Nationals, regardless of LTV / CLTV, need to document a minimum of 60 days seasoning.” Whether the repatriation requirement applies to any borrower holding funds abroad or only to foreign nationals, and what evidence applies: Acra confirmation requested → Q-12. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

ledger.clause:
STD-9.6 The sources state reserves only for the situations below, and state the payment basis only where shown. The base requirement where no trigger applies, the payment basis where only “months” is stated, permitted sources, whether overlapping triggers are cumulative, and whether reserves substituted for rent loss insurance are additional: Acra confirmation requested → Q-07. \[S; G\]

| **Trigger** | **Reserves as printed** | **Source** |
|----|----|----|
| LTV \> 80.00% | 6 months PITIA reserves | S: Income Documentation |
| FICO \< 620 | 12 Months | S: Credit Requirements |
| First-time homebuyer | Minimum six months reserves (“Requires 6mos Reserves”) | G §3.13; S: Restrictions |
| Vacant property — rate & term refinance | Minimum six months reserves | G §10.17; S: Occupancy Type |
| Vacant property — cash-out refinance | 6 months reserves | S: Occupancy Type |
| Property listed for sale within six months | Twenty-four (24) months of reserves; cash-in-hand may be considered if otherwise consistent with the Guide | G §11.5 |
| Forbearance or mortgage lates in the last 12 months, tenant-occupied subject, without timely receipt of the prior two months' rent | 12 months of the subject's payment in reserve, which may be from the transaction's cash-in-hand | G §5.32 |
| Rent loss insurance required but cannot be obtained | Two (2) months reserves for every one (1) month of coverage not provided | G §23.40 |

condition.purpose: Determine whether the required entity documents are complete and meet the stated requirements.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the entity documents and identification for the required formation, governance, ownership, qualification, tax-identification, and transaction-authorization documents.

Final Determination: Determine whether the required entity documentation meets the stated requirements.

rule.description: Verify the required entity documentation and its stated contents.

ledger.clause:
STD-6.10 The documents below are required, without exception, and borrower letters stating that they are not required, available, or excused from providing such documents are not acceptable. \[G §3.12, pp. 8–9\]

- Complete, legible copy of the Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization and all amendments thereto.

- Complete (with all referenced exhibits), legible copy of the Operating Agreement for LLCs and Partnerships, or Bylaws for corporations, and all amendments, that states whether the entity is member or manager managed, contains authorization to borrow money and enter into contracts for mortgage assets, and designates signers. Additional information may be required if the formation documents and the Operating Agreement or Bylaws conflict.

- All documentation evidencing ownership interests: for LLCs and Partnerships, the Operating Agreement must identify, or attach as an exhibit, all persons by name with their ownership interest, or provide copies of the membership interest certificates / units in compliance with the Operating Agreement.

- For S or C Corporations: shareholder / stockholder certificates that comply with the Bylaws, if any, or, if stock certificates are lost or unavailable, the corporation's stock ledger. The certificate or ledger must account for all outstanding shares noted in the Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization, including those held by the corporation. If stock certificates are lost, destroyed, mutilated, or otherwise unavailable, an Affidavit of Lost Stock Certificate is required.

- For S-corporations or Partnerships, where both stock certificate and stock ledger are unavailable: (i) the most recent preceding tax year's K-1 statement for all members with 20% or more interest, and (ii) a letter from the CPA or Tax Preparer affirming current ownership interest, with a statement to that effect if the preceding year's taxes have not been filed.

- Names on the entity documents must match the identification; if they do not match exactly, a letter of explanation is required to address the discrepancy.

- Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent document valid within ninety (90) days of the closing date.

- Certificate of Foreign Qualification or other qualification to operate in the state where business is being conducted, if the entity is formed in a state other than where business is performed or where the property is located.

- IRS Form SS4 or Federal Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) or Employer Identification Number (EIN) issuance letter for the entity. EIN exception requests may be submitted for review by Acra's Legal Department with a letter of explanation stating the applicable grounds.

- A Unanimous Written Consent / Board Resolution signed by all members regardless of their percentage of interest, (i) authorizing the transaction with Acra Lending and (ii) identifying who is authorized to sign the loan documents on behalf of and to bind the entity. It may be required by the Operating Agreement or Bylaws even where ownership is held by one individual. It cannot be used to designate a signor on a personal guarantee, only an authorized signor for the loan documents signed by the entity.

- A Power of Attorney must be utilized by the principal to designate an attorney in fact to execute a personal guarantee; see §23.5(C), not reproduced (Appendix B).

- Legal reserves the right to condition for additional supporting documentation as determined in its sole discretion.

ledger.clause:
STD-5.6 Assets held / foreign accounts must be verified in U.S. Dollar equivalency at the current exchange rate via www.xe.com or the Wall Street Journal conversion table. \[G §3.10, p. 6\]

STD-5.7 Sufficient funds to close must be on deposit with the Escrow / Closing Agent at least three (3) business days (including Saturdays for this calculation) prior to any closing date. \[G §3.10, p. 6\]

STD-5.8 A copy of the two (2) most recent statements of that account is required. If the funds are not seasoned a minimum of sixty (60) days, a letter of explanation is required along with the information to comprise a sixty (60) day chain of funds. Bank statements in any language other than English must be translated into English. \[G §3.10, p. 6\]

STD-5.9 Per §8.4, Foreign Nationals, regardless of LTV / CLTV, need to document a minimum of 60 days seasoning, and funds held in a foreign bank / currency must be repatriated at minimum three (3) business days prior to Closing (STD-9.5). \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

STD-9.1 Gift funds, investment property or second homes: applicant(s) are required to contribute a portion of their own sourced and seasoned funds to the transaction at a minimum of 10% of the purchase price. Gift documentation requirements are in the Seller's Guide gift-fund section (Appendix B). \[G §8.7, p. 12; S: Loan Amount\]

STD-9.2 Verification of the seasoning of funds to close is required on loans over 70% CLTV for consumer transactions, or business purpose loans where funds to close are over \$50,000 and over 70% CLTV. Whether any loan on this program is a consumer transaction: Acra confirmation requested → Q-27. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

STD-9.3 Where the account(s) serving as the source of funds must be verified, verification may include a copy of the borrower's bank statement(s) for the most recent month(s), or a VOD reflecting a current and average balance for the most recent month(s). \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

STD-9.4 “All transactions require a minimum of 30-days documentation.” Whether any seasoning period applies to domestic funds beyond this documentation minimum: Acra confirmation requested → Q-12. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

STD-9.5 “In contrast to the above, but consistent with §3.10.1 of this Guide, funds held in a foreign bank / currency will need to be repatriated at minimum three (3) business days prior to Closing and Foreign Nationals, regardless of LTV / CLTV, need to document a minimum of 60 days seasoning.” Whether the repatriation requirement applies to any borrower holding funds abroad or only to foreign nationals, and what evidence applies: Acra confirmation requested → Q-12. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

condition.purpose: Check the printed maximum CLTV for short sale, deed-in-lieu, and modification seasoning bands.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the loan application and credit information for short sale, deed-in-lieu, or modification history, seasoning, loan purpose, and CLTV.

Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Compare seasoning and loan purpose with the printed table: ≥ 24 Mo, No Restrictions; 12-23 Mo, 80% purchase / 75% refinance; < 12 Mo, 75% purchase / 70% refinance.

Step 4 - Final Determination: Record whether the applicable printed restriction is met. Treat “FB Taken ≤6 Mos: Case-by-case” as requiring a case-by-case determination; the meaning and timing are subject to Acra confirmation → Q-05.

For seasoning < 12 Mo, CLTV is no more than 75% for purchase or 70% for refinance — rate & term and cash-out.

outcomes.criterion: The applicable printed seasoning restriction is met.

ledger.clause:
- Names on the entity documents must match the identification; if they do not match exactly, a letter of explanation is required to address the discrepancy.

- Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent document valid within ninety (90) days of the closing date.

- Certificate of Foreign Qualification or other qualification to operate in the state where business is being conducted, if the entity is formed in a state other than where business is performed or where the property is located.

- IRS Form SS4 or Federal Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) or Employer Identification Number (EIN) issuance letter for the entity. EIN exception requests may be submitted for review by Acra's Legal Department with a letter of explanation stating the applicable grounds.

- A Power of Attorney must be utilized by the principal to designate an attorney in fact to execute a personal guarantee; see §23.5(C), not reproduced (Appendix B).

- Legal reserves the right to condition for additional supporting documentation as determined in its sole discretion.

condition.purpose: Determine whether a calculated DSCR meets the stated minimum for each applicable situation.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the DSCR calculation and information identifying the loan amount, credit file, property, occupancy, purpose, and borrower status.

Eligibility Verification: Identify each applicable situation: LTV above 80.00%; loan amount over $2,000,000; 1 or no score / deficient tradelines; rural / unique property; non-warrantable condo or condotel / PUDtel; first-time homebuyer; vacant-property rate & term refinance; vacant-property cash-out refinance; property listed for sale within six months; or mixed use, adult care or assisted living.

Validation and Verification: Verify the calculated DSCR against each applicable stated minimum: 1.20 for LTV above 80.00%; 1.0 for loan amount over $2,000,000; 1.1 for 1 or no score / deficient tradelines; 1.00 for rural / unique property; 1.0 for non-warrantable condo or condotel / PUDtel; 1.150 for first-time homebuyer; 1.000 for vacant-property rate & term refinance; 1.15 for vacant-property cash-out refinance; 1.0 for property listed for sale within six months; and 1.2 for mixed use, adult care or assisted living.

Final Determination: Record whether the calculated DSCR meets every minimum that applies. The stated DTI alternatives for vacant-property rate & term refinance and properties listed for sale are not resolved here; Acra confirmation is requested on those provisions.
checks: If LTV is above 80.00%, calculated DSCR is at least 1.20.
If the loan amount is over $2,000,000, calculated DSCR is at least 1.0.
If there is 1 or no score / deficient tradelines, calculated DSCR is at least 1.1.
If the property is rural / unique, calculated DSCR is at least 1.00.
If the property is a non-warrantable condo or condotel / PUDtel, calculated DSCR is at least 1.0.
If the borrower is a first-time homebuyer, calculated DSCR is at least 1.150.
If the property is vacant and the transaction is a rate & term refinance, calculated DSCR is at least 1.000.
If the property is vacant and the transaction is a cash-out refinance, calculated DSCR is at least 1.15.
If the property was listed for sale within six months, calculated DSCR is at least 1.0.
If the property is mixed use, adult care or assisted living, calculated DSCR is at least 1.2.

outcomes.criterion: A calculated DSCR is established and meets every applicable minimum listed in the checks.
There is no case for this outcome.
A calculated DSCR is below an applicable minimum, or an applicable minimum cannot be established as met.
None of the listed situations applies.

STD-3.16 LTV \> 80.00%: requires a minimum DSCR of 1.20 and 6 months PITIA reserves; limited to SFR, Warrantable Condos outside of Florida, Townhome, PUD. Stated in LTV where the matrix is labelled CLTV: Acra confirmation requested → Q-17. \[S: Income Documentation\]

STD-3.17 DSCR \< 1.0 or No Ratio: maximum CLTV 75% (purchase), 70% (refinance — rate & term), 65% (refinance — cash-out); minimum FICO 640. \[S: Income Documentation\]

STD-3.18 “The minimum rental income required is outlined in the Program Matrix.” The minimum ratios stated for particular situations across both sources are collected below; each is also stated in its own section. \[G §5.32, p. 3\]

| **Situation** | **Minimum DSCR as stated** | **Source** |
|----|----|----|
| LTV above 80.00% | 1.20 | S: Income Documentation |
| Loan amount over \$2,000,000 | 1.0 | S: Loan Amount |
| 1 or no score / deficient tradelines | 1.1 | S: Credit Requirements |
| Rural / unique property | 1.00 | S: Subject Property Location |
| Non-warrantable condo; condotel / PUDtel | 1.0 | S: Subject Property Type |
| First-time homebuyer | 1.150 | G §3.13; S: Restrictions |
| Vacant property, rate & term refinance | 1.000 (“OR Maximum 40.0% DTI” — Q-14) | G §10.17; S: Occupancy Type |
| Vacant property, cash-out refinance | 1.15 | S: Occupancy Type |
| Property listed for sale within six months | 1.0 (“or (b) 43% maximum DTI” — Q-14) | G §11.5 |
| Mixed use, adult care or assisted living | 1.2 | G §10.7 |

STD-4.9 “Acra defines a First Time Home Buyers (‘FTHB’) as an application where all Applicants have never previously owned a home (real property).” \[G §3.13, p. 10\]

STD-4.10 DSCR: Acra allows first-time homebuyers under all of the following: minimum 700 FICO score; maximum 70% CLTV; minimum DSCR of 1.150; maximum loan amount of \$1,000,000; full amortization required, no interest-only programs; impounds required; minimum six months reserves. The Summary states the same conditions: “Minimum 700 FICO: Max 70% CLTV: DSCR ≥ 1.15: Loan amt ≤ \$1MM: NO I/O: Must Impound: Requires 6mos Reserves”. \[G §3.13, p. 10; S: Restrictions\]

STD-4.11 “Where a FTHB is purchasing an Investment property and the loan is qualifying via DTI program, the maximum DTI will be 43.0%.” Noted as a DTI-program provision — Q-14. \[G §3.13, p. 10\]

STD-4.12 §3.12 separately requires at least one guarantor with prior homeownership experience where the borrower is an entity (STD-6.9). How that requirement and the first-time-homebuyer allowance interact: Acra confirmation requested → Q-09.

STD-8.1 Eligible property types: SFR, Townhome, PUD, Warrantable Condo, Non-Warrantable Condo, Condotel / PUDtel, 2-4 Units, Manufactured. Restrictions as printed: \[S: Subject Property Type\]

| **Property type** | **Purchase** | **Refi R/T** | **Refi C/O** | **Conditions as printed** |
|----|----|----|----|----|
| Non-Warrantable Condo | 80% | 75% | 75% | “-5% CLTV for Florida properties, Min DSCR: 1.0” |
| Condotel / PUDtel | 75% | 70% | 65% | “-5% CLTV for Florida properties Min DSCR: 1.0” |
| 2-4 Unit | 80% | 80% | 80% | Printed as “Max CLTV: 80%” with no purpose split |
| Manufactured Home | 65% | 60% | 60% | — |

STD-8.2 Above 80.00% LTV only SFR, Warrantable Condos outside of Florida, Townhome and PUD are eligible (STD-3.16). \[S: Income Documentation\]

STD-8.3 Rural / unique property: maximum CLTV 80% (purchase), 75% (refinance — rate & term), 70% (refinance — cash-out); minimum FICO 700; minimum DSCR 1.00. “If marketing time is excessive or property exhibits unusual, inadequate or peculiar functionality, LTV may be further reduced.” \[S: Subject Property Location\]

STD-8.4 Declining market: “-5% CLTV property/borrower full profile” (STD-1.14). \[S: Subject Property Location\]

STD-8.5 A vacant property may be purchased; qualifying rents are taken from the 1007 or 1025 (STD-3.8). “Vacant investment properties are only eligible for a refinance transaction if consistent with §10.17.” \[G §5.32, p. 3; §3.41, p. 11\]

STD-8.6 Rate and term refinance of a vacant property (§10.17): minimum 700 FICO score; maximum \$1,000,000 to maximum 70% CLTV; maximum \$2,000,000 to maximum 65% CLTV; minimum 1.000 DSCR or maximum 40.0% DTI (Q-14); minimum two-year prepayment penalty (where allowable); full amortization required, no interest-only programs; impounds required; minimum six months reserves. The Summary states the same conditions with “Max CLTV 70% for loan amounts under \$1,000,000 and 65% for loan amounts under \$2,000,000”. Treatment at exactly \$1,000,000 and \$2,000,000: Acra confirmation requested → Q-10. \[G §10.17, p. 11; S: Occupancy Type\]

STD-8.7 Cash-out refinance of a vacant property: the “Cash-Out Refinances” heading in §10.17 is empty in the excerpt. The Summary states: minimum 700 FICO; DSCR ≥ 1.15; ≥ 3-year PPP (where allowable); no interest only; impounds required; 6 months reserves; “Max CLTV 60% for loan amounts under \$1,500,000”; “Requires ≥15 months ownership”. Loans of \$1,500,000 or more, and how the 15 months are measured: Acra confirmation requested → Q-10. \[S: Occupancy Type; G §10.17, p. 11\]

STD-8.8 A property is considered listed for sale under §11.5 if it has been listed for sale in the last six months, measured from (a) the last date of being listed to (b) the Application Date. \[G §11.5, p. 12\]

STD-8.9 Loans on such properties will be considered under the following characteristics: the property is not in default or otherwise delinquent on lien(s); for investment properties, the subject must be occupied by a tenant and may not be vacant; the loan must qualify as either (a) ≥ 1.0 DSCR or (b) 43% maximum DTI (Q-14); a prepayment penalty of at least three (3) years is required unless the property is in a state that does not allow prepayment penalties; twenty-four (24) months of reserves are required, and cash-in-hand may be considered if otherwise consistent with the Guide; the loan must have a fully amortizing term, interest only is not available; the maximum LTV / CLTV is 65% based on the lesser of (a) appraised value or (b) lowest recent listing price; no subordinate financing is allowed; impounds are required. \[G §11.5, pp. 11–12\]

STD-8.10 A mixed-use property has a portion of its space dedicated to commercial use and the rest dedicated to residential use. Acra may approve mixed use properties under the conditions outlined in §10.7, which also holds all restrictions regarding Adult Care / Assisted Living Facilities; these properties require a minimum DSCR ratio of 1.2. §10.7 is not reproduced (Appendix B). \[G §10.7, p. 12\]

steps: Initial Document Review: Review the rental-income and property-expense information used for the calculation.

condition.purpose: Determine whether the documentation stated for actual rents exceeding market rents is present.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the actual-rent and market-rent information, rental-income receipt evidence, and lease agreement(s).

condition.purpose: Determine whether six (6) months' rent loss insurance is required for the subject property under the stated property, LTV, and rent-qualification conditions.

STD-6.1 Business Entities are eligible for financing on business purpose transactions (investment properties exclusively). \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.2 Acra will lend to, and require that title to the collateral be held, either (i) directly by an individual person(s) or (ii) by an entity acceptable to Acra in its sole discretion. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.3 Acra requires all individuals with direct or indirect ownership ≥ 20% to provide a recourse guarantee (Acra approved, or Exhibit 7) in the case of an entity borrower. All recourse is joint and several in the case of multiple guarantors. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.4 An entity borrower must be a single purpose entity (SPE): “an entity with no assets other than residential investment or rental properties; engaged in the business of owning and operating residential investment or rental properties.” Series limited liability companies are not allowed. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.5 All entities that will hold direct ownership of the subject property and will be on title as a direct owner are required to be a borrowing entity. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.6 Changes to the operating agreement or bylaws with the intent of changing ownership percentages to circumvent required personal guarantors will not be considered. “Lookback to changes cannot occur within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process as these changes will not be recognized by Acra Lending.” \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.7 Entity / guarantor types allowed: Domestic Corporations (C and S Corp); single purpose Limited Liability Companies (LLC), excluding series LLC; Limited Liability Partnership (LLP); Limited Liability Limited Partnership (LLLP); General Partnership (GP); Limited Partnership (LP); and Sole Proprietorship. “In all events, the Borrower must be a US formed and based Entity, foreign entities (i.e.: entities formed or based outside the US) or foreign owned entities are not allowed.” \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

STD-6.8 Not allowed: Cooperatives, Irrevocable Trusts, Land Trusts, IRAs, Non-Profit, and Joint Ventures. “Business entity nesting is limited to only one (1) wholly-owned subsidiary that in turn must be owned by individual(s); multiple nesting or ownership by multiple entities, trusts, etcetera are not acceptable.” An illustration of the permitted structure: Acra confirmation requested → Q-22. \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

See Q-09. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether a Foreign National meets the stated residence and transaction-purpose requirements and apply the published CLTV limits.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the loan_application and supporting borrower documentation for residence, authorization to live or work in the U.S., and transaction purpose.

Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Apply the stated Foreign National CLTV maximums: 70% for purchase and 65% for refinance — rate & term and cash-out. Verify the loan is priced at FICO equal to 700.

condition.purpose: Determine whether an interest-only loan meets the applicable published product and eligibility conditions.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the loan_application, credit_report, and appraisal_report for interest-only term, product, loan amount, FICO, CLTV, and property and borrower characteristics.

Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Confirm the selected product is one of the published eligible interest-only products: 5 Yr / 30 year term on 5/1 or 7/1 ARM; 5 Yr / 30 Year Fixed; or 10 Yr / 40 Year Term.

Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Apply minimum loan amount $250,000 and minimum 640 credit score. For 10 Yr / 40 Year Term, also apply maximum 80% LTV / CLTV and maximum $3M loan amount. Interest-only is not available to first-time homebuyers, on vacant-property refinances, or on properties listed for sale.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Determine whether the applicable interest-only product conditions are met.
checks: The selected interest-only product is a published eligible product.
The loan amount is at least $250,000 and FICO is at least 640.
For 10 Yr / 40 Year Term, loan amount does not exceed $3M and LTV / CLTV does not exceed 80%.
The borrower is not a first-time homebuyer.
The loan is not a refinance of a vacant property.
The property is not listed for sale.

The excerpt's DTI calculation for interest-only loans (first fully amortized payment on the original balance; for an ARM, the highest achievable rate at that payment's due date) is a DTI-program provision — Q-14. \[G §7.5, p. 13\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether the stated mixed-use minimum DSCR is met and identify the additional unreproduced conditions.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the appraisal_report and loan_application for commercial and residential use of the property.
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Verify whether a portion of the property's space is dedicated to commercial use and the rest to residential use.

Step 3 - Validation and Verification: For a mixed-use property, apply minimum DSCR ratio of 1.2 and identify that approval conditions in §10.7, including restrictions regarding Adult Care / Assisted Living Facilities, are not reproduced in the source.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Determine whether the minimum DSCR is met and refer unreproduced §10.7 conditions for review.

condition.purpose: Determine whether the selected structure is published and meets stated transaction-specific minimum terms.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the loan_application for property state, transaction type, unit count, borrower or entity closing name, loan amount, interest rate, and selected prepayment penalty structure.

Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Verify that the selected structure is one of the published structures: 5 Year 5% Fixed or Sequential Stepdown; 4 Year 5% Fixed or 3% Fixed; 3 Year 5% Fixed or 3% Fixed; 2 Year 3% Fixed; 1 Year 3% Fixed; or No Prepay.

Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Apply stated minimums: vacant-property rate & term refinance requires at least two years and vacant-property cash-out refinance at least three years, each where allowable; property listed for sale requires at least three years unless located in a state that does not allow prepayment penalties. Apply the printed state restrictions as written; the meaning of “BUY-OUT” and how state restrictions interact with the minimums require Acra confirmation.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Determine whether the selected structure meets applicable stated minimums and refer unresolved state-restriction interpretation for confirmation.
checks: The selected prepayment penalty structure is one of the published structures.
A vacant-property rate & term refinance has a prepayment penalty of at least two years where allowable.
A vacant-property cash-out refinance has a prepayment penalty of at least three years where allowable.
A property listed for sale has a prepayment penalty of at least three years unless the property is in a state that does not allow prepayment penalties.
Any applicable printed state restriction is reviewed and any unresolved “BUY-OUT” interpretation or interaction with a stated minimum is referred for Acra confirmation.

outcomes.criterion: The selected structure is published, every applicable minimum is met, and applicable state restrictions are resolved.
An applicable minimum remains uncleared or an applicable state restriction requires Acra confirmation.
The selected structure is not published or an applicable stated minimum is not met.
No prepayment penalty requirement applies to the case.

Acra confirmation of what “BUY-OUT” requires and how a state restriction interacts with stated minimum terms.

condition.purpose: Determine whether a property listed within the stated period meets the applicable loan conditions.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review listing_history, loan_application, appraisal_report, and relevant lien and underwriting records for listing dates, occupancy, value, and loan terms.
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Treat a property as listed for sale if it was listed in the last six months, measured from the last date of being listed to the Application Date.

Step 3 - Validation and Verification: For a covered loan, verify that the property is not in default or delinquent on liens; an investment property is tenant-occupied and not vacant; qualification is ≥ 1.0 DSCR or 43% maximum DTI; PPP is at least three (3) years unless the property is in a state that does not allow prepayment penalties; reserves are twenty-four (24) months; the loan is fully amortizing and not interest only; maximum LTV / CLTV is 65% based on the lesser of appraised value or lowest recent listing price; no subordinate financing is allowed; and impounds are required.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Determine whether the applicable listed-property conditions are met.
checks: The property was listed for sale within the last six months as measured from the last listing date to the Application Date.
The property is not in default or otherwise delinquent on lien(s).
For an investment property, the subject is occupied by a tenant and is not vacant.
The loan qualifies as either ≥ 1.0 DSCR or 43% maximum DTI.
The loan has a prepayment penalty of at least three (3) years unless the property is in a state that does not allow prepayment penalties.
Reserves are twenty-four (24) months.
The loan is fully amortizing and is not interest only.
LTV / CLTV does not exceed 65% based on the lesser of appraised value or lowest recent listing price.
No subordinate financing is allowed and impounds are required.

outcomes.criterion: The property is listed within the stated period and every applicable listed-property condition is met.
Evidence or a condition needed to determine or clear an applicable listed-property requirement remains outstanding.
An applicable listed-property condition is not met.
The property was not listed for sale in the last six months under the stated measurement.

condition.purpose: Calculate DSCR with annual real estate taxes included in the denominator.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Gather the data needed for the DSCR calculation: annual in-place rent, market rent, the annual denominator amounts, and the first payment due under the terms of the Note. Identify whether the loan is interest-only.

Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Use the lesser of annual in-place rent or market rent as the numerator. Include annual principal, interest, real estate taxes, property insurance, and homeowner's / condominium association fees in the denominator; include subordinate financing if applicable.

Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Divide the numerator by the denominator. If the loan is interest-only, obtain Acra confirmation of which payment enters the denominator. Apply the market rent reference §14.14 only when its applicable method is available; it is not reproduced in the excerpt.

Step 4 - Final Determination: Record the DSCR only when the required amounts and applicable calculation basis are available. Do not treat the subordinate-financing calculation rule as establishing that subordinate financing is permitted.
checks: The numerator is the lesser of annual in-place rent or market rent.
The denominator includes annual principal, interest, real estate taxes, property insurance, and homeowner's / condominium association fees.
Subordinate financing is included in the denominator if applicable.
The DSCR is the numerator divided by the denominator.
The first payment due under the terms of the Note is used, subject to Acra confirmation of the payment basis for an interest-only loan.

outcomes.criterion: Every step is met and every check holds, with the applicable market rent method and, for an interest-only loan, Acra confirmation available.
The calculation is subject to obtaining data needed for the formula, the applicable §14.14 market rent method, or Acra confirmation of the denominator payment basis for an interest-only loan.
A step is not met or a check does not hold, including when the calculation omits annual real estate taxes from the denominator.
There is no case for this outcome.

ledger.clause:
STD-3.1 “Acra calculates the DSCR by dividing (a) the lesser of (i) annual in-place rent or (ii) market rent (reference §14.14) by (b) the sum of annual principal, interest, real estate taxes, property insurance, and homeowner's / condominium association fees (collectively, ‘PITIA’). Subordinate financing, if applicable, would also be included in the denominator for the sake of this calculation.” \[G §5.32, p. 3\]

STD-3.2 “Acra calculates the DSCR utilizing the first payment due under the terms of the Note.” §7.5 defines Interest Only payments as “the amount sufficient to pay the accrued interest to the mortgage on a monthly basis at the time of origination”, while the §5.32 denominator lists “annual principal, interest …”. Which payment enters the DSCR denominator on an interest-only loan: Acra confirmation requested → Q-26. \[G §7.5, p. 13; §5.32, p. 3\]

STD-3.3 The reference to subordinate financing in the denominator is a calculation rule; it does not itself establish that a subordinate lien is permitted. Whether and when subordinate financing is permitted: Acra confirmation requested → Q-18. \[G §5.32, p. 3\]

STD-3.4 §14.14 (market rent), referenced in the formula, is not reproduced in the excerpt (Appendix B). \[G §5.32, p. 3\]

ledger.clause:
STD-6.13 Title vesting in an inter vivos revocable trust is permitted when all of the following requirements are followed. \[G §3.12, pp. 9–10\]

- A complete, legible copy of the Trust, or a Certification of Trust stating: the existence and date of the Trust; the Trustor(s) and the current Trustee(s); the powers of the Trustee; whether the Trust is revocable and, if revocable, who holds the right to revoke; the names and number of the Trustees required to sign on behalf of the Trust; the Trust identification number (a Social Security number or an IRS-issued Tax Identification Number); how title to the Trust assets should be taken; and a statement that the Trust has not been revoked, modified, or amended in any manner.

STD-6.1 Business Entities are eligible for financing on business purpose transactions (investment properties exclusively). \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.5 All entities that will hold direct ownership of the subject property and will be on title as a direct owner are required to be a borrowing entity. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.6 Changes to the operating agreement or bylaws with the intent of changing ownership percentages to circumvent required personal guarantors will not be considered. “Lookback to changes cannot occur within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process as these changes will not be recognized by Acra Lending.” \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.7 Entity / guarantor types allowed: Domestic Corporations (C and S Corp); single purpose Limited Liability Companies (LLC), excluding series LLC; Limited Liability Partnership (LLP); Limited Liability Limited Partnership (LLLP); General Partnership (GP); Limited Partnership (LP); and Sole Proprietorship. “In all events, the Borrower must be a US formed and based Entity, foreign entities (i.e.: entities formed or based outside the US) or foreign owned entities are not allowed.” \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

ledger.clause:
STD-6.13 Title vesting in an inter vivos revocable trust is permitted when all of the following requirements are followed. \[G §3.12, pp. 9–10\]

- A complete, legible copy of the Trust, or a Certification of Trust stating: the existence and date of the Trust; the Trustor(s) and the current Trustee(s); the powers of the Trustee; whether the Trust is revocable and, if revocable, who holds the right to revoke; the names and number of the Trustees required to sign on behalf of the Trust; the Trust identification number (a Social Security number or an IRS-issued Tax Identification Number); how title to the Trust assets should be taken; and a statement that the Trust has not been revoked, modified, or amended in any manner.

- The Trust must be valid under the laws of the state in which it is established.

- The Trust must be revocable, meaning it can be changed or canceled at any time for any reason during a Trustor's lifetime. Irrevocable trust is not permitted.

- The Trust must be established by one or more natural persons, solely or jointly (Grantor, Trustor, or Settlor), and must become effective during the lifetime of the person(s) establishing it.

- The primary beneficiary of the Trust must be the individual(s) establishing the Trust.

- Written exception by Acra Senior Management must be obtained if the Trustor(s) and Trustee(s) are not the same.

- The Trust must specify that the Trustee has the power to hold title and mortgage the property; that the beneficiary does not need to grant written consent for the Trust to borrow money, or that such consent has been granted in writing for purposes of the mortgage; that there is no unusual risk or impairment to the lender's rights; and that holding title in the Trust does not diminish the lender's rights as a creditor.

- Legal reserves the right to condition for additional supporting documentation as determined in its sole discretion.

- A complete, legible copy of the Trust, or a Certification of Trust stating: the existence and date of the Trust; the Trustor(s) and the current Trustee(s); the powers of the Trustee; whether the Trust is revocable and, if revocable, who holds the right to revoke; the names and number of the Trustees required to sign on behalf of the Trust; the Trust identification number (a Social Security number or an IRS-issued Tax Identification Number); how title to the Trust assets should be taken; and a statement that the Trust has not been revoked, modified, or amended in any manner.

- The Trust must be valid under the laws of the state in which it is established.

- The Trust must be revocable, meaning it can be changed or canceled at any time for any reason during a Trustor's lifetime. Irrevocable trust is not permitted.

- The Trust must be established by one or more natural persons, solely or jointly (Grantor, Trustor, or Settlor), and must become effective during the lifetime of the person(s) establishing it.

- The primary beneficiary of the Trust must be the individual(s) establishing the Trust.

- Written exception by Acra Senior Management must be obtained if the Trustor(s) and Trustee(s) are not the same.

- The Trust must specify that the Trustee has the power to hold title and mortgage the property; that the beneficiary does not need to grant written consent for the Trust to borrow money, or that such consent has been granted in writing for purposes of the mortgage; that there is no unusual risk or impairment to the lender's rights; and that holding title in the Trust does not diminish the lender's rights as a creditor.

- Legal reserves the right to condition for additional supporting documentation as determined in its sole discretion.

ledger.clause:
STD-6.1 Business Entities are eligible for financing on business purpose transactions (investment properties exclusively). \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.2 Acra will lend to, and require that title to the collateral be held, either (i) directly by an individual person(s) or (ii) by an entity acceptable to Acra in its sole discretion. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.3 Acra requires all individuals with direct or indirect ownership ≥ 20% to provide a recourse guarantee (Acra approved, or Exhibit 7) in the case of an entity borrower. All recourse is joint and several in the case of multiple guarantors. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.4 An entity borrower must be a single purpose entity (SPE): “an entity with no assets other than residential investment or rental properties; engaged in the business of owning and operating residential investment or rental properties.” Series limited liability companies are not allowed. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.5 All entities that will hold direct ownership of the subject property and will be on title as a direct owner are required to be a borrowing entity. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.6 Changes to the operating agreement or bylaws with the intent of changing ownership percentages to circumvent required personal guarantors will not be considered. “Lookback to changes cannot occur within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process as these changes will not be recognized by Acra Lending.” \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.7 Entity / guarantor types allowed: Domestic Corporations (C and S Corp); single purpose Limited Liability Companies (LLC), excluding series LLC; Limited Liability Partnership (LLP); Limited Liability Limited Partnership (LLLP); General Partnership (GP); Limited Partnership (LP); and Sole Proprietorship. “In all events, the Borrower must be a US formed and based Entity, foreign entities (i.e.: entities formed or based outside the US) or foreign owned entities are not allowed.” \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

ledger.clause:
PLAT-3.1 “When calculating the DSCR, Acra will use the greater of the market rent as established on the 1007 or 1025, or actual rent. When using actual rent, the actual rent must be documented via evidence of 2 months’ proof of receipts and the lease must be in place for at least 3 months after the loan closing. This applies to long-term rents only and is not appropriate for short-term rentals.” \[P: Income Documentation & Debt Ratio Requirements\]

PLAT-3.2 §5.32 of the excerpt states the general formula as “the lesser of (i) annual in-place rent or (ii) market rent”, then notes that “Acra may use the higher of actual or market rents” subject to “two (2) consecutive months proof of rental income receipt”, a lease continuing at least three months after closing, and: “Security Deposit does not count towards receipt, and the rents cannot be prepaid.” The Platinum Summary's statement (PLAT-3.1) is program-specific; the excerpt's general formula is reproduced here. Which governs Platinum Select and how they relate, whether “2 months’ proof of receipts” means consecutive months, and whether the security-deposit and prepaid-rent conditions apply: Acra confirmation requested → Q-03. \[G §5.32, p. 3\]

PLAT-3.3 Short-term rentals are ineligible for the program (PLAT-7.2); the Seller's Guide provisions on short-term rental income and appraisal forms are not restated (Appendix B). \[P: Subject Property Requirements\]

condition.purpose: Establish that the required entity documentation has been provided without exception, subject to the stated EIN exception process and Legal's right to condition for additional documentation.
steps: Initial Document Review: Collect and review the entity's formation documents and amendments; Operating Agreement with referenced exhibits for LLCs and Partnerships or Bylaws for corporations and amendments; ownership-interest evidence; applicable stock certificates, stock ledger, K-1 statements, CPA or Tax Preparer letter, and Affidavit of Lost Stock Certificate; identification; Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent; applicable foreign qualification; IRS Form SS4, TIN, or EIN issuance letter; Unanimous Written Consent / Board Resolution; and any required Power of Attorney.

Eligibility Verification: Confirm the required documents are provided without relying on borrower letters stating that documents are not required, available, or excused. Confirm that applicable Operating Agreements or Bylaws state whether the entity is member or manager managed, authorize borrowing money and entering into contracts for mortgage assets, and designate signers.

Validation and Verification: Verify legibility, completeness, required ownership information, matching names or a letter of explanation, Certificate of Good Standing validity within ninety (90) days of the closing date, applicable foreign qualification, and the required authorization and signer information. Apply the stated ownership-evidence requirements for LLCs, Partnerships, S or C Corporations, and the stated S-corporation or Partnership fallback when both stock certificate and stock ledger are unavailable. An EIN exception request may be submitted for review by Acra's Legal Department with a letter of explanation stating the applicable grounds. Do not use a Unanimous Written Consent / Board Resolution to designate a signor on a personal guarantee. Obtain a Power of Attorney when a principal designates an attorney in fact to execute a personal guarantee. Refer additional supporting-documentation requests to Legal as applicable.
Final Determination: Determine whether the required entity documentation has been provided and meets the applicable stated requirements.
checks: The required entity documents are provided, complete, legible, and satisfy the applicable content, ownership, name, timing, qualification, authorization, and signer requirements.

rule.description: Verify the required entity documents are complete, legible, applicable, and meet the stated content and timing requirements.

ledger.clause:
PLAT-5.10 The documents below are required, without exception, and borrower letters stating that they are not required, available, or excused from providing such documents are not acceptable. \[G §3.12, pp. 8–9\]

- Complete, legible copy of the Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization and all amendments thereto.

- Complete (with all referenced exhibits), legible copy of the Operating Agreement for LLCs and Partnerships, or Bylaws for corporations, and all amendments, that states whether the entity is member or manager managed, contains authorization to borrow money and enter into contracts for mortgage assets, and designates signers. Additional information may be required if the formation documents and the Operating Agreement or Bylaws conflict.

- All documentation evidencing ownership interests: for LLCs and Partnerships, the Operating Agreement must identify, or attach as an exhibit, all persons by name with their ownership interest, or provide copies of the membership interest certificates / units in compliance with the Operating Agreement.

- For S or C Corporations: shareholder / stockholder certificates that comply with the Bylaws, if any, or, if stock certificates are lost or unavailable, the corporation's stock ledger. The certificate or ledger must account for all outstanding shares noted in the Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization, including those held by the corporation. If stock certificates are lost, destroyed, mutilated, or otherwise unavailable, an Affidavit of Lost Stock Certificate is required.

- For S-corporations or Partnerships, where both stock certificate and stock ledger are unavailable: (i) the most recent preceding tax year's K-1 statement for all members with 20% or more interest, and (ii) a letter from the CPA or Tax Preparer affirming current ownership interest, with a statement to that effect if the preceding year's taxes have not been filed.

- Names on the entity documents must match the identification; if they do not match exactly, a letter of explanation is required to address the discrepancy.

- Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent document valid within ninety (90) days of the closing date.

- Certificate of Foreign Qualification or other qualification to operate in the state where business is being conducted, if the entity is formed in a state other than where business is performed or where the property is located.

- IRS Form SS4 or Federal Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) or Employer Identification Number (EIN) issuance letter for the entity. EIN exception requests may be submitted for review by Acra's Legal Department with a letter of explanation stating the applicable grounds.

- A Unanimous Written Consent / Board Resolution signed by all members regardless of their percentage of interest, (i) authorizing the transaction with Acra Lending and (ii) identifying who is authorized to sign the loan documents on behalf of and to bind the entity. It may be required by the Operating Agreement or Bylaws even where ownership is held by one individual. It cannot be used to designate a signor on a personal guarantee, only an authorized signor for the loan documents signed by the entity.

- A Power of Attorney must be utilized by the principal to designate an attorney in fact to execute a personal guarantee; see §23.5(C), not reproduced (Appendix B).

- Legal reserves the right to condition for additional supporting documentation as determined in its sole discretion.

rule.description: Verify that title vesting in an inter vivos revocable trust meets each stated trust requirement.

ledger.clause:
PLAT-5.13 Title vesting in an inter vivos revocable trust is permitted when all of the following requirements are followed. \[G §3.12, pp. 9–10\]

- A complete, legible copy of the Trust, or a Certification of Trust stating: the existence and date of the Trust; the Trustor(s) and the current Trustee(s); the powers of the Trustee; whether the Trust is revocable and, if revocable, who holds the right to revoke; the names and number of the Trustees required to sign on behalf of the Trust; the Trust identification number (a Social Security number or an IRS-issued Tax Identification Number); how title to the Trust assets should be taken; and a statement that the Trust has not been revoked, modified, or amended in any manner.

- The Trust must be valid under the laws of the state in which it is established.

- The Trust must be revocable, meaning it can be changed or canceled at any time for any reason during a Trustor's lifetime. Irrevocable trust is not permitted.

- The Trust must be established by one or more natural persons, solely or jointly (Grantor, Trustor, or Settlor), and must become effective during the lifetime of the person(s) establishing it.

- The primary beneficiary of the Trust must be the individual(s) establishing the Trust.

- Written exception by Acra Senior Management must be obtained if the Trustor(s) and Trustee(s) are not the same.

- The Trust must specify that the Trustee has the power to hold title and mortgage the property; that the beneficiary does not need to grant written consent for the Trust to borrow money, or that such consent has been granted in writing for purposes of the mortgage; that there is no unusual risk or impairment to the lender's rights; and that holding title in the Trust does not diminish the lender's rights as a creditor.

- Legal reserves the right to condition for additional supporting documentation as determined in its sole discretion.

condition.purpose: Determine whether the property is subject to the listed-for-sale requirements and whether each stated characteristic is met.

Interest only is not available.

Step 4 - Final Determination: Record whether the six-month trigger applies and whether every applicable stated characteristic is met. Do not resolve the stated Q-13 or Q-14 questions without confirmation.

ledger.clause:
The Platinum Summary lists two eligible citizenship types and excludes first-time homebuyers. Borrowing entities, guarantors and trusts follow the Seller's Guide excerpt and are in section 5.

PLAT-4.1 Eligible borrower citizenship types: US Citizen, Permanent Resident. \[P: Borrower Citizenship Requirements\]

PLAT-4.2 Permanent Resident must have an unexpired PRA ID and SSA card / SSA-89. \[P: Borrower Citizenship Requirements\]

PLAT-4.3 Non-permanent residents, foreign nationals and ITIN borrowers are not among the listed eligible types. The Seller's Guide foreign-national program (§3.10) is therefore not restated (Appendix B). \[P: Borrower Citizenship Requirements\]

PLAT-4.4 “First Time Homebuyer (FTHB) ineligible for this program”. Acra defines a First Time Home Buyer as “an application where all Applicants have never previously owned a home (real property)”; the §3.13 DSCR allowance for first-time homebuyers is not restated (Appendix B). \[P: Borrower Credit History Requirements; G §3.13, p. 10\]

PLAT-4.5 §3.12 requires at least one guarantor to have prior homeownership experience, and at least one borrower / guarantor to attest on the application that they are not a first-time homebuyer (PLAT-5.9). Whether it applies to individual borrowers as well as entities is part of Q-13. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

condition.purpose: Establish whether the entity borrower has provided the required entity documentation.
steps: Initial Document Review: For an entity borrower, review the entity documents. Verify a complete, legible Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization and all amendments. Verify a complete, legible Operating Agreement for LLCs and Partnerships, or Bylaws for corporations, with all referenced exhibits and amendments. The Operating Agreement or Bylaws must state whether the entity is member or manager managed, contain authorization to borrow money and enter into contracts for mortgage assets, and designate signers. Verify documentation evidencing ownership interests: for LLCs and Partnerships, the Operating Agreement must identify by name all persons with their ownership interest, or attach that information as an exhibit, or provide membership interest certificates / units in compliance with the Operating Agreement. For S or C Corporations, verify shareholder / stockholder certificates that comply with the Bylaws, if any, or the stock ledger if certificates are lost or unavailable; the certificate or ledger must account for all outstanding shares noted in the formation document, including those held by the corporation. If stock certificates are lost, destroyed, mutilated, or otherwise unavailable, verify an Affidavit of Lost Stock Certificate. For S-corporations or Partnerships where both stock certificate and stock ledger are unavailable, verify the most recent preceding tax year's K-1 statement for all members with 20% or more interest and a letter from the CPA or Tax Preparer affirming current ownership interest, with a statement to that effect if the preceding year's taxes have not been filed.

Eligibility Verification: Verify that names on entity documents match the identification; if they do not match exactly, verify a letter of explanation addressing the discrepancy. Verify a Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent valid within ninety (90) days of the closing date. If the entity is formed in a state other than where business is performed or where the property is located, verify a Certificate of Foreign Qualification or other qualification to operate in the state where business is being conducted. Verify IRS Form SS4 or a Federal Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) or Employer Identification Number (EIN) issuance letter for the entity. An EIN exception request may be submitted for review by Acra's Legal Department with a letter of explanation stating the applicable grounds. Verify a Unanimous Written Consent / Board Resolution signed by all members regardless of their percentage of interest, authorizing the transaction with Acra Lending and identifying who is authorized to sign the loan documents on behalf of and to bind the entity. Check whether it is required by the Operating Agreement or Bylaws even where ownership is held by one individual. It cannot designate a signor on a personal guarantee, only an authorized signor for the loan documents signed by the entity. If a Power of Attorney is used to designate an attorney in fact to execute a personal guarantee, verify that it is utilized by the principal; see §23.5(C), not reproduced (Appendix B).

Validation and Verification: Do not accept borrower letters stating that required documents are not required, available, or excused from providing such documents. If the formation documents and the Operating Agreement or Bylaws conflict, additional information may be required. Legal reserves the right to condition for additional supporting documentation as determined in its sole discretion.

Final Determination: Record whether all required documentation applicable to the entity and the stated document-specific requirements have been verified, and identify any outstanding conditions or additional information requested.
checks: The complete, legible formation document and all amendments are provided.
The applicable Operating Agreement or Bylaws and all referenced exhibits and amendments meet the stated requirements.
The applicable documentation evidencing ownership interests is provided and meets the stated requirements.
The applicable corporate share documentation is provided and meets the stated requirements, including an Affidavit of Lost Stock Certificate when required.
For an S-corporation or Partnership where both stock certificate and stock ledger are unavailable, the required K-1 statements and CPA or Tax Preparer letter are provided.
Entity document names match identification, or a letter of explanation addresses any exact-name discrepancy.
A Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent valid within ninety (90) days of the closing date is provided.
If applicable, a Certificate of Foreign Qualification or other qualification to operate in the state where business is being conducted is provided.

IRS Form SS4 or a Federal Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) or Employer Identification Number (EIN) issuance letter is provided, or an EIN exception request with a letter of explanation stating the applicable grounds is submitted for review by Acra's Legal Department.
The required Unanimous Written Consent / Board Resolution is provided and meets the stated requirements.
If a Power of Attorney is used to designate an attorney in fact to execute a personal guarantee, it is utilized by the principal.
No borrower letter states that required documents are not required, available, or excused from providing such documents.

PLAT-5.10 The documents below are required, without exception, and borrower letters stating that they are not required, available, or excused from providing such documents are not acceptable. \[G §3.12, pp. 8–9\]

- Complete, legible copy of the Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization and all amendments thereto.

- Complete (with all referenced exhibits), legible copy of the Operating Agreement for LLCs and Partnerships, or Bylaws for corporations, and all amendments, that states whether the entity is member or manager managed, contains authorization to borrow money and enter into contracts for mortgage assets, and designates signers. Additional information may be required if the formation documents and the Operating Agreement or Bylaws conflict.

- All documentation evidencing ownership interests: for LLCs and Partnerships, the Operating Agreement must identify, or attach as an exhibit, all persons by name with their ownership interest, or provide copies of the membership interest certificates / units in compliance with the Operating Agreement.

- For S or C Corporations: shareholder / stockholder certificates that comply with the Bylaws, if any, or, if stock certificates are lost or unavailable, the corporation's stock ledger. The certificate or ledger must account for all outstanding shares noted in the Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization, including those held by the corporation. If stock certificates are lost, destroyed, mutilated, or otherwise unavailable, an Affidavit of Lost Stock Certificate is required.

- For S-corporations or Partnerships, where both stock certificate and stock ledger are unavailable: (i) the most recent preceding tax year's K-1 statement for all members with 20% or more interest, and (ii) a letter from the CPA or Tax Preparer affirming current ownership interest, with a statement to that effect if the preceding year's taxes have not been filed.

- Names on the entity documents must match the identification; if they do not match exactly, a letter of explanation is required to address the discrepancy.

- Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent document valid within ninety (90) days of the closing date.

- Certificate of Foreign Qualification or other qualification to operate in the state where business is being conducted, if the entity is formed in a state other than where business is performed or where the property is located.

- IRS Form SS4 or Federal Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) or Employer Identification Number (EIN) issuance letter for the entity. EIN exception requests may be submitted for review by Acra's Legal Department with a letter of explanation stating the applicable grounds.

- A Unanimous Written Consent / Board Resolution signed by all members regardless of their percentage of interest, (i) authorizing the transaction with Acra Lending and (ii) identifying who is authorized to sign the loan documents on behalf of and to bind the entity. It may be required by the Operating Agreement or Bylaws even where ownership is held by one individual. It cannot be used to designate a signor on a personal guarantee, only an authorized signor for the loan documents signed by the entity.

- A Power of Attorney must be utilized by the principal to designate an attorney in fact to execute a personal guarantee; see §23.5(C), not reproduced (Appendix B).

- Legal reserves the right to condition for additional supporting documentation as determined in its sole discretion.

ledger.clause:
PLAT-3.1 “When calculating the DSCR, Acra will use the greater of the market rent as established on the 1007 or 1025, or actual rent. When using actual rent, the actual rent must be documented via evidence of 2 months’ proof of receipts and the lease must be in place for at least 3 months after the loan closing. This applies to long-term rents only and is not appropriate for short-term rentals.” \[P: Income Documentation & Debt Ratio Requirements\]

PLAT-3.2 §5.32 of the excerpt states the general formula as “the lesser of (i) annual in-place rent or (ii) market rent”, then notes that “Acra may use the higher of actual or market rents” subject to “two (2) consecutive months proof of rental income receipt”, a lease continuing at least three months after closing, and: “Security Deposit does not count towards receipt, and the rents cannot be prepaid.” The Platinum Summary's statement (PLAT-3.1) is program-specific; the excerpt's general formula is reproduced here. Which governs Platinum Select and how they relate, whether “2 months’ proof of receipts” means consecutive months, and whether the security-deposit and prepaid-rent conditions apply: Acra confirmation requested → Q-03. \[G §5.32, p. 3\]

PLAT-3.3 Short-term rentals are ineligible for the program (PLAT-7.2); the Seller's Guide provisions on short-term rental income and appraisal forms are not restated (Appendix B). \[P: Subject Property Requirements\]

ledger.clause:
PLAT-3.1 “When calculating the DSCR, Acra will use the greater of the market rent as established on the 1007 or 1025, or actual rent. When using actual rent, the actual rent must be documented via evidence of 2 months’ proof of receipts and the lease must be in place for at least 3 months after the loan closing. This applies to long-term rents only and is not appropriate for short-term rentals.” \[P: Income Documentation & Debt Ratio Requirements\]

PLAT-3.2 §5.32 of the excerpt states the general formula as “the lesser of (i) annual in-place rent or (ii) market rent”, then notes that “Acra may use the higher of actual or market rents” subject to “two (2) consecutive months proof of rental income receipt”, a lease continuing at least three months after closing, and: “Security Deposit does not count towards receipt, and the rents cannot be prepaid.” The Platinum Summary's statement (PLAT-3.1) is program-specific; the excerpt's general formula is reproduced here. Which governs Platinum Select and how they relate, whether “2 months’ proof of receipts” means consecutive months, and whether the security-deposit and prepaid-rent conditions apply: Acra confirmation requested → Q-03. \[G §5.32, p. 3\]

PLAT-3.3 Short-term rentals are ineligible for the program (PLAT-7.2); the Seller's Guide provisions on short-term rental income and appraisal forms are not restated (Appendix B). \[P: Subject Property Requirements\]

PLAT-3.4 Denominator, per §5.32: “the sum of annual principal, interest, real estate taxes, property insurance, and homeowner's / condominium association fees (collectively, ‘PITIA’). Subordinate financing, if applicable, would also be included in the denominator for the sake of this calculation.” \[G §5.32, p. 3\]

PLAT-3.5 “Acra calculates the DSCR utilizing the first payment due under the terms of the Note.” §7.5 defines Interest Only payments as “the amount sufficient to pay the accrued interest to the mortgage on a monthly basis at the time of origination”, while the §5.32 denominator lists “annual principal, interest …”. Which payment enters the DSCR denominator on an interest-only loan: Acra confirmation requested → Q-21. \[G §7.5, p. 13; §5.32, p. 3\]

PLAT-3.6 The reference to subordinate financing in the denominator is a calculation rule; it does not itself establish that a subordinate lien is permitted. The Platinum Summary does not address subordinate financing or restate the Standard Summary's HELOC calculation: Acra confirmation requested → Q-15. \[G §5.32, p. 3\]

rule.description: Verify the listed entity eligibility and required entity documentation for an entity borrower.

ledger.clause:
PLAT-5.1 Business Entities are eligible for financing on business purpose transactions (investment properties exclusively). \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.2 Acra will lend to, and require that title to the collateral be held, either (i) directly by an individual person(s) or (ii) by an entity acceptable to Acra in its sole discretion. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.3 Acra requires all individuals with direct or indirect ownership ≥ 20% to provide a recourse guarantee (Acra approved, or Exhibit 7) in the case of an entity borrower. All recourse is joint and several in the case of multiple guarantors. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.4 An entity borrower must be a single purpose entity (SPE): “an entity with no assets other than residential investment or rental properties; engaged in the business of owning and operating residential investment or rental properties.” Series limited liability companies are not allowed. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.5 All entities that will hold direct ownership of the subject property and will be on title as a direct owner are required to be a borrowing entity. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.6 Changes to the operating agreement or bylaws with the intent of changing ownership percentages to circumvent required personal guarantors will not be considered. “Lookback to changes cannot occur within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process as these changes will not be recognized by Acra Lending.” \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.7 Entity / guarantor types allowed: Domestic Corporations (C and S Corp); single purpose Limited Liability Companies (LLC), excluding series LLC; Limited Liability Partnership (LLP); Limited Liability Limited Partnership (LLLP); General Partnership (GP); Limited Partnership (LP); and Sole Proprietorship. “In all events, the Borrower must be a US formed and based Entity, foreign entities (i.e.: entities formed or based outside the US) or foreign owned entities are not allowed.” \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

PLAT-5.8 Not allowed: Cooperatives, Irrevocable Trusts, Land Trusts, IRAs, Non-Profit, and Joint Ventures. “Business entity nesting is limited to only one (1) wholly-owned subsidiary that in turn must be owned by individual(s); multiple nesting or ownership by multiple entities, trusts, etcetera are not acceptable.” An illustration of the permitted structure: Acra confirmation requested → Q-18. \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

PLAT-5.9 Acra requires at least one guarantor to have prior homeownership experience. At least one (1) borrower / guarantor on the loan must attest on the application that they are not a first-time homebuyer; if prior home ownership is not evident within the loan file, the underwriter reserves the right to condition for supporting documentation. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]
